model_note: RTO Limited is NOT a growth-DCF candidate. It is a dormant NZX Main Board cash shell with NO operating business, NO revenue (FY2026 'total income' of $70,031 is $69,000 of one-off reimbursement income plus $1,031 of bank interest - neither is repeatable operating revenue), and NEGATIVE owner FCF in every year on record since the mortgage-lending business was discontinued in FY2023. A discounted-cash-flow model built on projected FCF would either extrapolate a business that does not exist or compound an unrepeatable cash-burn trajectory into a meaningless negative valuation. This model instead values the equity as a probability-weighted mix of (a) shareholder-support failure / wind-up (bear), (b) continued life-support with an eventual, heavily-dilutive reverse takeover (RTO) that leaves existing holders with tangible book value plus a modest listed-shell scarcity premium (base), and (c) a prompt, favourable-terms RTO realizing the shell's option value near the top of observed NZX shell-value precedent (bull). This mirrors the structural approach used for the comparable NZX distressed shell AFC.NZ and this company's own prior model under its old BGI.NZ ticker (see research/BGI.NZ/Reports/BGI.NZ_DCF.json), carried forward unchanged in methodology - the ONLY substantive change in this refresh is correcting current_price from a dead $0.004 BGI.NZ quote to the live $0.118 RTO.NZ quote and recomputing every price-dependent figure (upside, entry-price discount, sanity-check multiples) accordingly. The underlying facts: no debt (bonds fully forgiven/converted in 2024) but a new $200,000 shareholder loan entered into after FY2026 year-end and expected to be advanced July 2026 (treated here as new, equity-subordinate debt/dilution risk, not free money), an explicit FY2026 auditor going-concern material-uncertainty paragraph (not yet a disclaimer of opinion), and a persistent multi-year pattern of management citing 'discussions with several potential acquisition targets' that has not converted into a signed transaction across at least three consecutive annual reports.

The $200,000 shareholder loan agreement entered into after balance date (expected advance July 2026) is NOT included in this FY2026-dated net-debt figure because it had not been drawn at 31 March 2026; it is instead treated qualitatively in the bear/base scenario narratives below as new debt that will rank ahead of equity once advanced, and as the funding mechanism that buys roughly one further year of runway.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Not applicable / deliberately omitted. There is no repeatable free cash flow to project - FY2026 operating cash outflow was -$173,632 (FY2025: -$346,307), funded entirely by drawing down the cash balance, and every dollar of 'income' is either token bank interest or a one-off reimbursement. Projecting this burn rate as a perpetuity or growth series would be fabricating precision the underlying business cannot support.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2026 net decrease in cash, shown for disclosure only. This is a cash-burn number, not an owner-earnings base - it is the OPPOSITE of a valuation input in the conventional DCF sense; a growing owner_fcf would normally support a HIGHER valuation, but for a shell every dollar of burn simply erodes the NTA floor the valuation actually rests on.
inputs.interest_income_note: Token bank interest on the shrinking cash balance ($1,031 in FY2026). Immaterial - not stripped or added back anywhere in this model because no FCF projection exists for it to distort.
inputs.sbc_source: Metrics.csv StockBasedComp column is blank/0 for every period FY2018-FY2026; no share-based payment expense has ever been disclosed. No SBC adjustment is required or meaningful for a non-operating shell with no employees beyond directors paid cash fees.
inputs.annual_share_growth_note: Held at 0% for the base/bear valuation arithmetic below because no specific RTO share-issuance ratio is disclosed (there is no MOU, term sheet, or announced transaction). Dilution from a completed RTO is instead handled qualitatively and structurally: the bull and base cases value the SHELL's retained economic claim directly (i.e., already net of the dilution existing holders would suffer issuing consideration shares to an RTO vendor), rather than modelling a specific new share count. This is the same treatment AFC.NZ used for its bull case.

inputs.nta_change_note: NTA per share nearly halved in one year (3.61c to 1.87c, -48%) purely from the operating loss - there is no operating business to have caused this via revenue or margin deterioration; it is pure cash-shell overhead burn.
inputs.cash_runway_note: $114,903 cash / $173,632 FY2026 burn rate = under 8 months of runway BEFORE the $200,000 shareholder loan. The going-concern basis of preparation depends explicitly on that loan (entered into after balance date, expected to be advanced July 2026) and on continued discretionary support thereafter - it is not optional financing, it is the difference between solvency and insolvency within the current fiscal year.
inputs.shareholder_loan_pending_note: $200,000 shareholder loan agreement with majority shareholder Blackwell Global Group Limited (BGGL), entered into after the 31 March 2026 balance date, expected to be advanced in July 2026. Not yet drawn as at the FY2026 balance date and therefore not in the FY2026 net-debt figure above, but explicitly relied upon by the directors for the going-concern basis of preparation. This is NEW DEBT ranking ahead of equity, not a grant - treated in the bear/base narratives as a real claim that will erode the residual equity value available to ordinary shareholders if the company does not find a transaction before the loan (and any successor funding) needs repaying or is converted (further diluting existing holders, as happened with the 2024 bond-to-equity conversion).
inputs.going_concern_note: Auditor William Buck (signed 24 June 2026) issued an unmodified opinion WITH an explicit 'Material Uncertainty Relating to Going Concern' paragraph (Note 24) - the going-concern basis is stated by the directors to depend on 'ongoing financial support from the majority shareholder, including a shareholder loan agreement of $200,000... entered into [and] expected to be advanced in July 2026' and on 'identifying a suitable business opportunity... and maintaining low operating costs.' This is one notch less severe than a full disclaimer of opinion (contrast AFC.NZ's two consecutive years of disclaimer), but is still an explicit, audited red flag that the entity's survival is not assured absent continued related-party support.
inputs.ownership_concentration_note: Blackwell Global Group Limited (BGGL) 74.08% + Mr Kaw (Michael) Sing Chai (the individual who controls BGGL) 7.59% personally = >81% combined control. Free float is a small residual of the register; daily trading volumes in the low single digits to low hundreds of shares (59 shares on the day this price was verified) confirm the stock is essentially untradeable in any size.
inputs.unrecognised_tax_losses_note: $3.89M of carried-forward tax losses, UNRECOGNISED on the balance sheet, and at real risk of forfeiture under shareholder-continuity rules if an RTO issues enough new shares to breach continuity thresholds - i.e., the very transaction that could realize the shell's option value could simultaneously destroy this asset. Not added to any scenario's equity value given this contingency and the fact it is unrecognised even by the company's own auditors.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Not applicable in the conventional sense. There has been no operating revenue since FY2023 (mortgage-lending business discontinued), so revenue and FCF CAGRs are null/not meaningful - there is no denominator-consistent series to compound. Shareholders' equity (NTA) CAGR is deeply NEGATIVE over 3 years (-41.8%, computed off equity of $0.950726m FY2023 -> $0.187125m FY2026) but near-FLAT over 5 years (-0.4%, computed off equity of $0.190764m FY2021 -> $0.187125m FY2026) purely because FY2021 was itself already a trough after the mortgage-lending wind-down began, not because the business stabilized - equity swung up to $0.951m (FY2023, post a capital injection) and back down to $0.167m (FY2024) and $0.187m (FY2026) in between. Neither CAGR is a meaningful growth-rate input: this is capital-structure noise (bond forgiveness, bond-to-equity conversion, the Aug-2024 consolidation) layered on a shrinking cash-shell overhead base, not compounding business performance. This is exactly why growth_rate_source is not_applicable and the valuation uses scenario-weighted asset value instead of a CAGR-driven DCF.
historical_growth.notes: No meaningful revenue, EPS, or FCF history exists to extrapolate. The only genuinely trending series is NTA per share, which nearly halved in FY2026 alone (3.61c to 1.87c) purely from overhead burn with no offsetting revenue. This is why the valuation approach below abandons growth-rate selection entirely in favour of scenario-weighted asset/option valuation.

base.narrative: The shell persists on continued shareholder life-support: the $200,000 BGGL loan is advanced as planned (July 2026), buying roughly another year of runway at the current burn rate, and the majority shareholder continues its established four-year pattern of funding overheads (debt forgiveness in 2024, equity conversion in 2024, now a direct loan in 2026) rather than letting the company fail outright. Eventually - not on any committed timeline - an RTO completes, but on terms that heavily dilute existing minority holders (consistent with a distressed, thinly-traded, >81%-controlled vehicle with limited negotiating leverage). Existing shareholders' residual claim approximates current tangible book value (NTA) plus a conservative NZX-listed-shell scarcity premium, consistent with the low end of observed precedent for a going-concern-qualified, unproven shell.
base.shell_scarcity_value_note: Uses the same NZ$0.5M anchor AFC.NZ's base case used for NZX shell-value precedent, chosen at the low end of the broader NZ$0.5-1.5M range cited there. RTO Limited's shell is of somewhat HIGHER quality than AFC.NZ's on some dimensions (only a going-concern material-uncertainty paragraph, not a two-year disclaimer of opinion; genuinely clean balance sheet with zero debt pre-loan; explicit board mandate/branding as an RTO vehicle) but LOWER on others (even thinner free float and liquidity, multi-year pattern of unconverted 'discussions' with no signed MOU or LOI disclosed at all - AFC.NZ at least had a named counterparty, Fast Track Group, at pre-MOU stage). These broadly offset, supporting the same NZ$0.5M base anchor.
base.burn_note: FY2027-FY2031 illustrative operating cash burn, shown for disclosure/schema completeness only. Funded in the base case by continued BGGL loans/support (the $200,000 already committed for July 2026, likely followed by further advances if no deal has landed, consistent with the 2024-2026 pattern). NOT subtracted a second time from the tangible-equity valuation above - as long as shareholder support continues, new debt/dilution is roughly a wash against the equity claim, which is the base case's core assumption. If that assumption fails, that is the bear case, not a modification of the base case.
base.discounting_note: No perpetuity cash-flow stream exists to discount (the burn is a funding wash against continued shareholder support, not a distributable return to equity). A WACC of 30% is disclosed for schema completeness and used only in the entry-price 15%-hurdle comparison context, not to discount a terminal FCF stream.

bull.narrative: A genuine, well-structured RTO completes reasonably promptly (within roughly 12-18 months) on terms favourable to existing holders - i.e. the incoming business is of real quality and existing shareholders retain a meaningful minority stake in a re-rated, operating public company, plus the clean listing and $3.89M of loss carryforwards (if continuity can be preserved) are genuinely monetized. This is explicitly speculative OPTION VALUE, not a cash-flow DCF output: there is no disclosed transaction structure, exchange ratio, letter of intent, MOU, or timeline as of the FY2026 annual report (24 June 2026). Management states only that it is 'hopeful of having a transaction underway during the course of this calendar year,' an aspiration repeated across multiple prior annual reports without conversion into a tangible deal.
bull.methodology_note: Uses the same NZ$2.5M upper-precedent anchor as AFC.NZ's bull case, representing the value of the shell/listing claim to existing shareholders PRIOR to dilution from newly issued RTO consideration shares - i.e. it approximates the aggregate retained economic exposure existing holders would have as minority stakeholders in a re-rated, real-business entity, without attempting to model a specific dilution ratio or the acquired business's own hypothetical cash flows (neither is disclosed, and cannot be, given no transaction has even reached the MOU stage). No new FCF projections are modelled for a hypothetical acquired business.

bear.narrative: No RTO materialises within a survivable timeframe. The board's multi-year pattern of citing 'discussions with several potential acquisition targets' (repeated, unconverted, across at least the FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026 annual reports) continues without a deal. The $200,000 BGGL loan is advanced as planned but merely extends the runway by roughly a year rather than solving the underlying problem; it also becomes a liability ranking AHEAD of equity. Either (a) BGGL eventually tires of open-ended funding and support lapses, forcing wind-up, with the loan and remaining payables paid out of the shrinking cash pile ahead of ordinary equity, leaving a token or nil residual; or (b) the company survives only via a heavily dilutive rescue placement/loan-to-equity conversion (as already happened once, in Aug-2024, when BGGL converted bonds to equity using Takeovers Code 'creep' provisions) that leaves today's minority holders with a small fraction of a smaller pie. Either path leaves ordinary equity holders with a small residual value, not zero (there is currently no debt and $114,903 of cash with no other creditors of scale), but severely impaired relative to today's NTA.
bear.residual_equity_value_note: Reflects cash and other assets net of the $200,000 loan repayment/conversion claim, wind-up/liquidation costs, and the near-certainty of a further dilutive raise or rescue transaction before any residual reaches ordinary holders. Not modelled as a literal zero (unlike AFC.NZ's bear case, which faced actual negative working capital and an audit disclaimer of opinion) because RTO Limited's FY2026 balance sheet is genuinely debt-free pre-loan and has no other material creditors - but the loan, once advanced, materially subordinates the equity claim, and the persistent failure to close any deal after years of 'discussions' is the single most probable outcome.
bear.burn_note: FY2027 burn includes the drawn shareholder loan being spent down; FY2028 support lapses or a rescue/wind-up event crystallizes the bear outcome.

base.funding_source: The $200,000 BGGL shareholder loan (expected July 2026), likely followed by further BGGL support consistent with the 2024-2026 pattern
base.note: Shown for transparency on the cost of continued life support only. Per the base-case methodology, this burn is funded externally (shareholder loan/further support) and is treated as a wash against the tangible-equity-plus-shell-premium valuation, not a further deduction from it.

bull.note: Only FY2027 pre-transaction burn/cost is shown. Post-RTO cash flows belong to an undisclosed acquired business and are not modelled; the bull intrinsic value is derived directly from shell-value precedent (see assumptions.bull), not from a discounted cash-flow sum.

bear.note: Loan drawn and spent down in FY2027; support lapses and a wind-up/heavily dilutive rescue event crystallizes the bear outcome by FY2028.

base.methodology: intrinsic_value = (FY2026 shareholders' equity/NTA + shell scarcity value) / shares outstanding = (187,125 + 500,000) / 10,000,026 = NZ$0.0687/share. Implies a P/NTA of 3.67x - well below the current market's 6.31x. At the live NZ$0.118 price, even the base case (a real, funded shell that eventually finds a deal on dilutive terms) implies roughly 42% downside.

bull.methodology: intrinsic_value = upper-precedent completed-RTO shell value / shares outstanding = 2,500,000 / 10,000,026 = NZ$0.2500/share. This is the ONLY one of the three scenarios that lands above the current NZ$0.118 price, and it requires a prompt, favourable-terms RTO completing - an outcome management has been unable to deliver despite citing 'discussions' across at least three consecutive annual reports. Assigned only 8% probability weight (see probability_weighted.weights_rationale).

bear.methodology: Residual equity value after the $200,000 shareholder loan (once advanced) is repaid/converted ahead of ordinary equity, wind-up or dilutive-rescue costs are applied, and no RTO materialises. intrinsic_value = 20,000 / 10,000,026 = NZ$0.0020/share.

entry_price.not_meaningful_note: A standard 15%-IRR entry-price formula assumes a cash-generating asset whose interim distributions plus a fair-value exit can be discounted back to a purchase price. RTO Limited generates no distributable cash flow (owner FCF has been negative in every year since the mortgage-lending business was discontinued in FY2023), pays no dividends, and its 'exit value' in every scenario is either near-zero (bear), a static book-value-plus-scarcity claim not expected to compound (base), or a binary, unpriced option contingent on an as-yet-unidentified counterparty and undisclosed terms (bull). Consistent with the AFC.NZ precedent, this section reports the probability-weighted intrinsic value itself as the decision-useful 'entry price' - the price at which a buyer pays exactly fair value across the three scenarios, with no presumption of a 15% return path because there is no modelled cash-flow stream to generate one.

recommended_entry_price.note: For this non-cash-flowing shell, the decision-useful 'entry price' is the probability-weighted fair value (see probability_weighted.weighted_iv) - the maximum price a rational buyer should pay given the realistic scenario mix, since no IRR-hurdle cash-flow mechanics apply. This is roughly 63% below the current NZ$0.118 (RTO.NZ) market price.

sensitivity.description: A standard WACC / terminal-growth grid is not meaningful here (no perpetuity cash-flow stream exists). Instead this matrix sensitizes the base-case intrinsic value to (rows) the haircut applied to FY2026 tangible NTA - reflecting uncertainty over whether even reported book equity is fully realizable in a forced scenario, given the company's total dependence on discretionary related-party funding - and (columns) the shell scarcity value assumption.
sensitivity.matrix_read_note: Row = NTA haircut (0% = full FY2026 book equity of NZ$187,125 credited; 100% = book equity assumed entirely unrealizable in a forced scenario). Column = shell scarcity value from NZ$0 (no RTO/promoter interest at all, i.e. pure liquidation) to NZ$1.0M (near the top of historical NZX shell-value precedent). At the live NZ$0.118 price, essentially NO cell in this matrix reaches the current price except the single top-right corner (zero haircut + NZ$1.0M shell value, NZ$0.1187/share) - an internally optimistic combination requiring BOTH crediting the full unhaircut book value AND assuming close to the maximum plausible shell premium simultaneously, not the modal outcome.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear is weighted heaviest (60%) given: (1) a cash runway of under 8 months at the FY2026 burn rate BEFORE the $200,000 shareholder loan, meaning survival is not currently self-funded; (2) the auditor's explicit Material Uncertainty Relating to Going Concern paragraph, which exists precisely because the directors' going-concern basis depends on discretionary, related-party support (the loan) rather than on any operating cash generation; (3) a persistent, multi-year pattern of management reporting 'discussions with several potential acquisition targets' (repeated across at least the FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026 annual reports, per the analysis JSON's recent_developments and guidance sections) with NONE converting into even a signed MOU or LOI, let alone a completed transaction - this is now a multi-year track record of non-delivery, not a one-off hopeful disclosure, and should be weighted accordingly rather than assuming the next attempt is more likely to succeed; (4) NTA per share nearly halving in a single year (3.61c to 1.87c, FY2025 to FY2026) shows the erosion is accelerating, not stabilizing; and (5) once advanced, the $200,000 shareholder loan is new debt that will rank ahead of ordinary equity, directly increasing the probability that any future rescue/dilution event leaves existing minority holders with little residual value - consistent with the 2024 precedent where BGGL used Takeovers Code 'creep' provisions to convert $250,000 of bonds into new shares at existing holders' expense (dilutively, from a minority perspective, even though it also cured a debt problem). Base (32%) reflects that Blackwell Global Group Limited has, to date, consistently chosen to keep funding the shell across multiple separate instances (the Apr-2024 and Aug-2024 bond forgiveness, the Aug-2024 equity conversion, and now the Jul-2026 loan commitment) rather than letting it lapse, so continued life-support long enough for SOME eventual transaction - even a heavily dilutive one - remains a real, non-trivial possibility. Bull (8%) reflects that a genuinely favourable-terms, prompt RTO remains possible in principle (the board is actively working the problem and the company markets itself explicitly as 'an attractive vehicle for a reverse takeover transaction'), but is assigned low weight because there is not even a disclosed MOU or LOI as of the most recent (24 June 2026) annual report, in contrast to even AFC.NZ's comparable bull case which at least had a named, pre-MOU counterparty (Fast Track Group). Weighting bull materially higher would require treating years of unconverted 'discussions' as a leading indicator of imminent success, which the disclosed track record does not support.

sanity_check.current_price_pnta_note: At the current RTO.NZ price of NZ$0.118, market cap is 0.118 x 10,000,026 = ~NZ$1.18M against FY2026 NTA of NZ$187,125 - an implied Price/NTA of ~6.31x. For a non-operating shell with no revenue and no EBITDA, the conventional multiple sanity checks (P/E, EV/EBITDA) do not apply - P/NTA (price to net tangible assets) is the only meaningful cross-check, and no asset-based method can justify NZ$0.118/share purely on book value: NTA alone is only NZ$0.0187/share. The roughly 6.3x gap between market price and NTA is not explained by any recognisable asset on the balance sheet - it is pure RTO/listed-shell option value, which is exactly what the probability-weighted scenario framework below is attempting to price, and which this model's central estimate (2.31x implied P/NTA) prices considerably more conservatively than the market currently does.
trip_reasons: The current price (NZ$0.118, P/NTA 6.31x) exceeds the top of this model's own scenario range in TWO of three scenarios (bear NZ$0.002, base NZ$0.069) and exceeds the probability-weighted intrinsic value (NZ$0.0432, implied P/NTA 2.31x) by roughly 173%.

Only the bull scenario (NZ$0.25, implied P/NTA 13.36x, 8% probability weight) lands above the current price - i.e. the market is pricing in bull-case-or-better odds of RTO success materially higher than this model's 8% weighting, given the multi-year pattern of unconverted deal discussions.

The going-concern material uncertainty and sub-8-month pre-loan cash runway are audited, disclosed facts as of the most recent (24 June 2026) annual report - they are not speculative bear-case inputs, they are the base state of the company today.

NTA per share nearly halved in the most recent fiscal year alone (3.61c to 1.87c) with no offsetting operating improvement possible (there is no operating business), meaning the book-value anchor underlying even the base and bull cases is itself on a declining trajectory absent a transaction.

The probability-weighted intrinsic value (NZ$0.0432) implies a P/NTA of only 2.31x - a materially more conservative multiple than the 6.31x the market currently pays, meaning this model's central estimate treats the market's RTO-optionality premium as substantially overpriced given the disclosed facts, not the other way round.
sanity_check.diagnosis: market pays a large premium for RTO optionality (~6.3x NTA) that this fundamentals-based scenario model does not match even after weighting a genuine (8%) chance of bull-case success; at NZ$0.118 the honest read is a large negative upside in the base and probability-weighted cases, and the gap is a judgment call on how likely a multi-year, still-undisclosed RTO search is to succeed, not a modelling error

valuation_philosophy.no_positive_fcf_history: There is no operating business and therefore no owner-FCF base to project. The mortgage-lending business was discontinued in FY2023; every year since has produced a net cash outflow funded by drawing down the cash balance (FY2025: -$346,307; FY2026: -$173,632), with 'income' consisting almost entirely of token bank interest and one-off reimbursements. Building a conventional DCF on this series would either extrapolate a business that no longer exists or compound a cash-burn trajectory into a nonsensical result. This is why the model uses an asset/scenario approach instead - the same fix applied to AFC.NZ and to this company's own prior BGI.NZ model.
valuation_philosophy.going_concern: The FY2026 audited financial statements (William Buck, signed 24 June 2026) contain an explicit Material Uncertainty Relating to Going Concern paragraph. The directors' stated basis for continuing as a going concern rests on 'ongoing financial support from the majority shareholder, including a shareholder loan agreement of $200,000... entered into [after balance date, and] expected to be advanced in July 2026' and on 'identifying a suitable business opportunity.' Cash of $114,903 against a $173,632 annual burn rate implies under 8 months of self-funded runway. That support is, by its nature, discretionary and can lapse or be renegotiated on terms unfavourable to existing minority holders at any time.
valuation_philosophy.value_rests_on_option_and_scarcity: To the extent this equity is worth more than its NTA, that excess value rests entirely on (a) a listed-shell scarcity premium to RTO promoters seeking a faster, cheaper route to an NZX Main Board listing than a traditional IPO, and (b) speculative, unpriced optionality on an as-yet-undisclosed reverse takeover actually being identified, negotiated, and completed on terms that leave existing holders with meaningful retained value after the near-certain heavy dilution such a transaction would require. Neither is a claim on any existing or currently foreseeable cash-generating business - there is none.
valuation_philosophy.market_pays_a_real_premium_this_model_on: RTO.NZ trades freely (last 251 daily bars through 13-Aug-2026, 52-week range NZ$0.118-$0.174) and has persistently commanded a multiple of NTA (currently ~6.3x) even as NTA itself has collapsed to under NZ$0.019/share. This is genuine, if thinly-traded (59 shares on the day this price was verified), price discovery reflecting real market appetite for RTO optionality in a >81%-controlled, going-concern-qualified nano-cap shell. This model's probability-weighted intrinsic value (NZ$0.0432, implied P/NTA 2.31x) sits materially below that market-implied multiple - a deliberately conservative read that treats years of unconverted 'discussions with several potential acquisition targets' as evidence the deal is genuinely uncertain, not imminent, rather than assuming the market's persistent premium is itself proof of an impending transaction.
valuation_philosophy.uninvestable_at_current_price_conclusion: At the current NZ$0.118 (RTO.NZ) price, this stock is priced for bull-case-or-better odds of a successful RTO that this model's fact base (a multi-year pattern of unconverted deal talk, an explicit going-concern qualification, under 8 months of pre-loan runway, and no disclosed MOU, LOI, or transaction terms) does not support assigning more than an 8% probability. The probability-weighted fair value (NZ$0.0432) is roughly 63% below the current price, and even the base case (a funded shell that eventually strikes a heavily dilutive deal) is roughly 42% below current price. No asset-based method - not even generous shell-value precedent stacked on top of full, unhaircut NTA - reaches NZ$0.118 without also assuming close to the maximum plausible shell premium simultaneously (see sensitivity.matrix_read_note). A rational buyer paying today's price is making a leveraged, largely binary bet that RTO Limited succeeds where it has not in at least three consecutive annual reporting cycles - not investing in a business with a demonstrable, ongoing path to that value.
